report_name: Oracle's October 2026 CPU Delivers Record 1,295 Security Patches

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: A significant number of the 95 critical vulnerabilities patched in Oracle's October 2026 CPU allow for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), enabling attackers to exploit systems over a network without credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: The advisory suggests monitoring for increased scanning or anomalous traffic on default Oracle service ports (1521, 7001, 3306) as a potential indicator of targeting.

vulnerabilities.name: Oracle October 2026 Critical Vulnerabilities
vulnerabilities.description: A batch of 95 critical vulnerabilities addressed in the Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update, many of which permit unauthenticated remote code execution. These vulnerabilities affect a wide range of Oracle products.

indicators.name: Anomalous Network Traffic on Oracle Service Ports
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Network Traffic on Oracle Service Ports
id: 7e8b1c2a-3d4e-4f5a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects network traffic to default ports for Oracle DB (1521), WebLogic (7001), and MySQL (3306). Increased scanning or anomalous traffic on these ports could indicate targeting of unpatched Oracle systems.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-25
references:
  - https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/cpuoct2026.html
tags:
  - attack.t1595
  - attack.reconnaissance
logsource:
  category: network_connection
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort:
      - '1521'
      - '7001'
      - '3306'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate traffic to these services.
level: low
indicators.description: Detects network traffic to default ports for Oracle DB (1521), WebLogic (7001), and MySQL (3306), which could indicate targeting of unpatched Oracle systems as suggested in the hunting hints.
